strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four benchmark collections (UCR-128, UEA-27, HAR, EEG) with strong and consistent results
Lightweight and computationally efficient model (2.2M parameters) substantially smaller than competitors while maintaining superior performance
Rigorous ablation studies (Sections B.1-B.7) systematically validate design choices including tokenizer components, architecture variants, and pre-training scheme
Novel layer-by-layer analysis providing valuable insights that intermediate representations unlock scaling benefits of pre-training
Sound technical approach to tokenization combining instance normalization, first-order differences, and patch-wise statistics
Excellent reproducibility prioritization with extensive implementation details and promised source code release
Thorough comparison with diverse baselines including self-supervised, tabular, forecasting, and vision-based foundation models
weaknesses: Misleading 'zero-shot feature extraction' terminology—linear probing on downstream task training data is few-shot adaptation, not zero-shot inference, undermining claimed contributions

Achieved SOTA results (0.862) heavily depend on multiple post-hoc test-time techniques (intermediate-layer selection, self-ensembling, cross-model fusion); baseline Mantis reaches only 0.8195, raising questions whether pre-training or inference tricks drive performance

Layer-wise model selection procedure uses downstream task labels to choose best layer for all models, violating zero-shot principles and enabling unfair comparison through task-aware feature selection
Limited fundamental novelty—individual components (transformers, contrastive learning, synthetic pre-training) are well-established; contribution is primarily engineering and combination
Modest absolute performance improvements over strong baselines (typically 1-3%), and self-ensembling adds substantial computational overhead contradicting 'lightweight' claims
Incomplete investigation of synthetic data generalization—unclear whether model learns artifacts specific to CauKer generation process or generalizes to real distributions unseen during pre-training
Fixed tokenization constraints (32 tokens, 512-length resizing) lack sensitivity analysis; no thorough investigation of how performance varies with actual sequence characteristics
Limited analysis of multivariate handling beyond brief adapter exploration, and inconsistent downstream classifiers (logistic regression vs Random Forest) complicate fair comparison

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse dataset collections (UCR-128, UEA-27, HAR, EEG) with detailed comparisons to 16+ baselines
Practical lightweight model with 2.2M parameters and fast inference, making deployment feasible
Extensive ablation studies and layer-by-layer analysis providing empirical insights (e.g., intermediate layers outperform final layers)
Strong zero-shot performance (0.8195 on UCR-128) competitive with or exceeding existing foundation models
Well-motivated problem: addressing the gap in classification-specific time series foundation models
Good reproducibility practices with detailed implementation details and hyperparameter specifications
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: tokenizer combines known techniques straightforwardly; contrastive learning and test-time optimizations are standard applications without methodological innovation

Heavy reliance on test-time engineering: best results (0.862) require accumulating multiple tricks (intermediate layers, token aggregation, self-ensembling, cross-model fusion); base model achieves only 0.8195

Methodological concerns: intermediate layer selection per-dataset risks overfitting; evaluation protocol changes between sections (logistic regression vs. Random Forest); no statistical significance testing despite marginal improvements
Synthetic pre-training analysis insufficient: limited justification for why 100K synthetic ≈ 1.89M real data; CauKer used as black box; generalization sensitivity unexplored
Misleading claims: 'zero-shot feature extraction' is standard linear probing; 'SOTA' requires combining with vision models; 'lightweight' requires larger models for best results
Lacks mechanistic insights: no explanation for why contrastive beats reconstruction, why intermediate layers outperform final layers, or why tokenizer design choices work beyond empirical observation
Incomplete comparison with NuTime: both pre-train on ~1.89M samples but Mantis claims 100K; dismisses fine-tuning unfairly despite Figure 18 showing improvements

Design choices inadequately justified: three tokenizer branches chosen without exploring alternatives; fixed 32 tokens justified only by 'computational constraints'; modern architecture components (RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU) provide marginal gains (~1%)

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap: most TSFMs focus on forecasting, not classification despite widespread TSC applications

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 diverse datasets (UCR-128, UEA-27, HAR, EEG) with thoughtful baseline coverage spanning self-supervised, tabular, forecasting, and vision models

Insightful empirical finding that intermediate layers consistently outperform final layers across multiple TSFMs in zero-shot regime—this generalizes beyond Mantis and is well-documented with layer-by-layer analysis
Lightweight and efficient model (2.2M parameters, inference speed comparable to handcrafted features) without sacrificing performance
Strong SOTA results on UCR (0.8195) with consistent improvements across diverse domains; avoids data leakage by using synthetic pre-training data
Thorough ablation studies validating each component; excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation details and promised source code
Multi-view tokenizer design combining raw signal, differential, and statistics is intuitive and empirically validated
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: token generator uses standard convolution+pooling, contrastive learning is conventional, and individual test-time techniques (self-ensembling, intermediate layers) are known. Contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Heavy reliance on test-time optimization: base model achieves 0.8195, but gains come mainly from self-ensembling (+0.0387) and cross-model fusion (+0.0425). This weakens core contribution claims and requires multiple forward passes, undermining the 'lightweight' narrative

Fairness concerns in comparisons: post-hoc intermediate layer analysis applied to all baselines (including those not designed for this) may advantage Mantis; modifying NuTime to remove its adapter may not represent optimal configuration; layer pruning improvements vary across models

Synthetic data dependency not fully explored: entirely dependent on CauKer with no comparison of alternative generators or sensitivity analysis; limited explanation of why synthetic data achieves parity with real data (Table 7)
Architecture design choices lack principled justification: why 32 tokens, 512 sequence length, 6 layers, kernel size 41? These appear determined empirically rather than through principled design
Multivariate handling is simplistic: channels processed independently then concatenated, ignoring cross-channel dependencies; adapters mentioned but treated as supplementary rather than core

Modest improvements over specialized baseline NuTime (0.8195 vs 0.7732 = +0.0463); gains over forecasting models larger but these weren't optimized for classification; TabPFN actually wins on short sequences (t<144)

Test-time mechanism interactions not analyzed: four techniques (intermediate layers, aggregation, self-ensembling, fusion) described separately but factorial combinations and interactions not explored
'Zero-shot' terminology is misleading: self-ensembling and cross-model fusion constitute test-time adaptation, weakening the zero-shot claim; really standard transfer learning via linear probing
Limited failure case analysis: no systematic discussion of when/why Mantis underperforms; EEG results show smaller improvements but this isn't analyzed in depth
